title: ANIME WORKOUTS - Would Jack Hanma's Transformation in Grappler Baki be possible
summary: Using Grappler Baki's 6'4" Jack Hanma as a case study, NH lists mistakes that keep tall skinny men small: too much cardio, overtraining, ignoring pain, chasing pump reps with poor form, and impatience. A natural transformation is possible with compounds, rep ranges of 3-9, recovery, calories, sleep and years of consistent work.
claims: Going from skinny to big is always possible naturally if the right parameters are met; believing you are destined to stay skinny is a lie
Skinny men prioritizing muscle should avoid cardio-focused activity, which burns calories needed to repair muscle and takes time from lifting
Skinny young men should focus on resistance training, especially compound exercises, which put the most muscle on the frame
Training beyond what you can recover from is useless and kills gains; muscle building is damage, then time and food to rebuild
Train enough to stimulate growth and progression with a strong focus on recovery; your goal is to get big, not to get good at working out
Muscles grow after training through supercompensation, not during; curls for five years nonstop without rest would never grow the biceps
Listen to pain: distinguish normal muscular soreness and pump from pain signaling potential injury or overtraining
Overtraining is a real threat for skinny lifters, trapping them in endless catabolism
Your muscular endurance baseline dictates your maximum recoverable volume; beyond it you waste time and rob the muscle of recovery time
If a drug cycle lets you keep the same training, the training was too harsh to ever work naturally
Set a rep range per exercise and work inside it to track volume and intensity; if you exceed the range, the weight was too light and you missed failure
Do not go home when you can no longer move; go home when the session is over and the muscles have been stimulated
Tall lanky lifters should focus on strength progression, staying between 2 and 15 reps with 3-9 as the core range
Tall lifters have longer trunks and limbs, so they must tune in to pain and not copy the technique of people five inches shorter
A session you can progress on and repeat frequently beats one that leaves you out for a week
Build a body that can eventually handle monstrous sessions; never start with them, and match the regimen to the body's demands
Lifters 6'2" or taller will eventually become monsters if they are patient
Without enough calories and sleep all the training in the world is useless for gaining mass
Steroids let Jack recover from a workload that was crushing him; naturals must instead build a body that grows into their ambitions over years
The taller and skinnier you start, the more space you have to fill, which takes years or decades, so avoid anything that threatens your ability to lift
Do not compare yourself to others or set arbitrary deadlines; obsessing over quick results leads to quitting
Ideals were never meant to be realistic; aiming for a manga physique is fine
Sustainability and frequency are key: there is no point getting jacked if it lasts two weeks
If you keep training and eating, you will get big; repeat that mantra daily
Start with about 40-minute sessions and increase density gradually, adding 10 minutes here and there as the body demands more work
